$comment: Machine-readable mirror of ledger-schema.md (the authoritative document). Update both in the same commit. Consumers: ledger-sync, future check tooling, agents that prefer structured data.
title: .context_ledger/ directory schema

core.sync: whole-tree, version-stamped, via ledger-sync update only

memory.sync: never — one deliberate exception: migrate/backfill group a legacy flat layout into memory/office/ (core 1.0.0)

history.sync: never; written only by ledger-history close
history.note: permanent accomplishments records (office-<NNN>.md, never deleted) + recently closed offices frozen verbatim (office-<NNN>/); never read at session start

archive.note: cold storage: office-<NNN>.tar.gz; capped by archive_keep, git-recoverable; the permanent record stays in history/

.context_ledger/kickoff.md.note: project data; regenerated by a session only when the template materially changes

officeFiles.$comment: The live office — memory/office/… — everything session-produced; frozen verbatim into history/office-<NNN>/ at close, next office starts from empty skeletons

STATE.md.note: single at-a-glance session digest — standing params, core version/drift, condensed roster, current task, backlog High rows, log entry counts, collaboration summary; regenerated at check-in and at exit; never hand-edited; read FIRST at session start in place of opening the individual files it summarizes

agents/sessions.md.note: current office's registry; frozen verbatim with the office at close

agents/roster.md.note: team roster for the current office; one row per person (Name, codename S<NNN>, model, doing, Status Working/Done/Blocked, Status detail — stage reached / shipped outcome / blocker); edit your own row in place as the work moves; Name and codename each unique; ledger-mem check enforces and warns on an empty Status cell; never reset or trimmed — the office is frozen verbatim at close with every shift intact; identity is claimed at check-in (fresh name + codename), never inferred from a model/harness-string match — model strings are shared across sessions, so duplicate model values are normal

tasks/current.md.note: single-agent lock only; collaboration mode uses event claims

tasks/backlog.md.note: actionable work only, capped (backlog_cap in history.conf, default 20); add a row to its priority table when an item can be started and finished, delete the row when it is finished or stale (completion record = session entry + commit); never delete a row whose work is still open and recorded nowhere else; past the cap, prune the lowest-value open row to the parking lot or delete it; non-actionable items (findings, questions, deferred, someday) go to tasks/parking-lot.md not here; ledger-mem check warns past the cap and closeout sweeps checked-off tombstones a session forgot to delete; at close only items with an active owner or a clear next step are re-seeded into the next office

tasks/parking-lot.md.note: the knowledge base, not a queue — research findings, open/advisory questions, deferred work, someday ideas; grouped by kind (Findings / Open questions / Deferred work / Someday), uncapped, no priority, no urgency; rows carry stable P-<date>-<n> IDs; promote an item to tasks/backlog.md when it becomes actionable (cut here, add a one-line row there), delete it when wrong or moot; not re-seeded wholesale at close — the closing session promotes what is now work and records the rest in the permanent record

plans/decisions.md.note: decisions still in force are re-seeded into the next office and recorded in the office's permanent record

sessions/SUMMARY.md.note: entries are removable; permanent record is agents/sessions.md

sessions/YYYY-MM-DD-N/notes.md.note: per-session detailed notes; disposable — durable facts must be promoted first

memoryFiles.$comment: Durable files at the memory/ root — orient a session, never rotate

collaboration/events/<event-id>.json.note: one file per peer event; never edit an event; legacy pre-0.22.0 <event-id>.md frontmatter files stay readable, never rewritten

workflows/active.md.note: protocol field is recorded 'by agent type', naming BOTH editions — never a single edition

workflows/gates.conf.note: explicit lifecycle commands; hybrid mode may discover conventional commands

workflows/history.conf.note: office rotation knobs: office_size (legacy key group_size still read), history_keep, archive_keep; backlog_cap (default 20) sizes the live work queue; flaws_cap/inefficiencies_cap (default 15 each) are hygiene nudges for ledger-mem check, not hard limits

overrides/rules.md.precedence: beats the edition, except secret-handling and append-only rules

office-<NNN>.md.writer: ledger-history close (filled by the closing session)
office-<NNN>.md.note: permanent accomplishments record: what the office achieved, decisions still in force, open threads re-seeded; never deleted, never gc'd

office-<NNN>/.note: the closed office, verbatim (roster with every shift, registry, notes, tasks, plans, logs, reviews); kept readable for history_keep offices, then zipped into archive/ and removed

legacy group-<NNN>.md.note: pre-1.0.0 condensed group records; left in place

office-<NNN>.tar.gz.note: the zipped frozen office; capped by archive_keep (gc deletes oldest-first, git-recoverable); the office's permanent record stays in history/

bindingRules.editionSelection: function of the running agent's type at session start; never read from memory
bindingRules.machineBlocks: apply only where the block's 'Identify by' matches
bindingRules.credentialFlows: agent-type facts; PAT steps exist only in the cloud edition
bindingRules.appendOnly: corrections are appended, never edited in; compaction is the sanctioned exception — byte-identical duplicates may be removed with a note, closed entries move verbatim into the log's archive.md, and 3+ entries hitting the same recurring thing roll up into one Recurring entry (instances archived verbatim); every moved line survives in the archive and in git history; ledger-mem prune reports sizes, eligible entries, and roll-up candidates; ledger-mem prune --apply performs the closed-entry moves mechanically (never the roll-up, which needs an agent's judgment); flaws_cap/inefficiencies_cap in history.conf (default 15) nudge ledger-mem check before a log grows unbounded
bindingRules.updateInPlace: one entry per key (ai-models.md keyed by Agent+Model, environments.md by its Identify-by line); correct an entry by editing it in place, never by appending a duplicate — the prior value survives in git history; ledger-mem check flags a duplicated key
bindingRules.officeLifecycle: one live office (memory/office/, unnumbered); ledger-history close freezes it verbatim — no condensing, no resetting — numbers it at that moment (derived from the records, no state file), writes the permanent accomplishments record, and opens a fresh empty office; the door trigger: a worker whose check-in read finds agents/sessions.md past office_size (default 20 — the codename they would claim is past S020) runs the close right after their check-in push, before the deep read — not skippable to 'finish this task first'; no implicit carryover — the closing session re-seeds open threads explicitly, re-seeded entries describe the work in plain words and never cite the closed office's session numbers or codenames (the permanent record bridges), and the new office's numbering starts clean (codenames from S001, entries from Session 1, ADRs and backlog IDs from 1); durable files at the memory root never rotate
bindingRules.oneWayLinkage: memory may reference product code; product code must never reference memory — no ADR number, bug ID, or .context_ledger/ path in a product docstring/comment/doc, which would be a dangling pointer for anyone reading only the product repo; ledger-mem lint flags it in the staged product diff and ledger-mem lint --tree sweeps every tracked product file; a leak found from an earlier session is stripped on sight (drop the reference, state any reason in plain words) as a safe fix, then the session continues — never tolerated, never backlogged
bindingRules.secrets: values only under memory/secrets/, never in tracked files, never echoed
bindingRules.coreReadOnly: no agent writes under .context_ledger/core/ in a project repo, ever
bindingRules.collaboration: peers are one team, not rivals; isolated worktree/branch per agent; the everyday event is an informal note (body-only, non-gating); a release/handoff closes a claim by citing its event ID or by sharing session+issue and overlapping paths; overlapping ACTIVE claims escalate to peers comparing changes and an agreement naming the best-supported option and one owner; no timestamp or agent-ID tie-breaker
bindingRules.collaborationCheck: ledger-collab check is the integration-readiness gate for malformed events, unresolved overlaps, incomplete agreements, unresolved corrections/handoffs, and releases without product commits; notes never gate it; single-pass so it stays fast on large trails
bindingRules.lifecycleGates: ledger-gates checkpoint runs before each next agent action; pre-commit, integration, and exit gates block their lifecycle transition on failure; explicit gates.conf commands take precedence over hybrid discovery; checkpoint warns (never blocks) when the office is full

commitPrefixes.officeClose: chore(ledger): close office-<NNN>, open a fresh office
